title: Artisan and enriched bread: control time and temperature

say: Artisan and enriched bread: control time and temperature.
This is the video for module four of Advanced Baking and Pastry.
Good bread is mostly about controlling time and temperature. Yeast is a living fungus. It works steadily at around 24 to 27 degrees.

say: It races in the heat, and dies at around 60 degrees. In a Nigerian kitchen above 30 degrees, the real skill is slowing yeast down.

say: She needs water at about 8 degrees, straight from the fridge. Her warm 30 degree dough used to rise in 45 minutes and tasted flat. At 25 degrees it takes about 90 minutes, and the flavour is clearly better.

say: Knead until the dough is smooth. Stretch a small piece. If light shows through without tearing, the gluten is ready.

panel.heading: Judge the dough, not the clock
items: Windowpane: stretches thin, lets light through
Bulk done: grown, domed, airy, wobbly
Over-fermented: alcohol smell, slack, tears
Divide by weight, allow for bake loss

say: Bulk fermentation is done when the dough has grown clearly, the top is domed with bubbles at the sides, and it wobbles when you move the container. The same dough can take twice as long on a cool morning.

panel.heading: Judge the dough, not the clock

Over-fermented: alcohol smell, slack, tears
Divide by weight, allow for bake loss

say: If it smells strongly of alcohol and tears easily, it has over-fermented. Next time use cooler water, less yeast or a shorter rise.

panel.heading: Judge the dough, not the clock

say: Always divide with a scraper and a scale. For example, Musa in Jos sells 400 gram loaves. His oven loses about 12 percent, so he divides at about 455 grams of dough.

say: Round each piece loosely and let it rest 15 to 20 minutes, so the gluten relaxes and the dough does not tear.

say: Shape it with tension, whether a round, an oval, a tin loaf or rolls. Cover it so a skin does not form.

say: Press a floured fingertip about 1 centimetre in. Springs back fast? Wait. Springs back slowly and leaves a small dent? Ready. Stays dented? Over-proofed. In a hot room, check early.

say: Steam burns as badly as boiling water. Pour water into the hot tray with a long-handled jug, keep your face and arms back, and wear dry oven gloves. Never use glass, because cold water can shatter it. Open the door slowly and stand to one side.

say: Enriched doughs add fat, sugar, eggs or milk. They are softer, but slower and stickier. For brioche, add the butter only after the gluten is developed, and keep the dough cool.

panel.heading: Soft milk bread with tangzhong
items: Tangzhong: 1 part flour, 5 parts milk
Cook to 65 C, then cool
Mix dough; add butter after gluten forms
Bake cooler, to 88 to 90 C inside

say: Tangzhong is a cooked paste that keeps bread soft for days. For example, Folake in Abeokuta uses 25 grams of flour, which is 5 percent of her 500, with 125 grams of milk.

say: Sugar, milk and eggs brown fast, so she bakes at about 175 degrees until the centre reads 88 to 90. Her loaves stay soft for three days. Cool them completely before bagging.

say: To remember. Work out your water temperature. Judge the rise by the dough, not the clock. Divide by weight.
Use the poke test before baking. And keep enriched doughs cool and bake them cooler.
